newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says President recovering well in Hanoi.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says President recovering well in Hanoi.

text.p: Vietnam's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that President Le Duc Anh was recovering well from illness and added he was still in Hanoi, apparently denying reports that he had been flown out of the country.
"As far as we know, President Le Duc Anh is still staying in Hanoi for a rest. His health recovery is going on well," the ministry said in a two-sentence statement.
Earlier, political sources said the 75-year-old general had been removed from a Hanoi army hospital, where he was in critical condition, and flown out of the country.
One said he had been admitted to a hospital in Singapore, which is where senior Hanoi officials with serious illnesses have been treated in the past.

The foreign ministry, asked about reports that Anh was in critical condition after suffering a stroke about 12 days ago, said on Tuesday that he was getting better. That was confirmed by one source, who said he had come out of a coma and was starting to look around him.
However, a scarcity of official comments about Anh's condition has sparked conflicting rumours in the streets and cafes of the capital.

Anh, who holds a key position of influence over the military and security apparatus, is part of a septuagenarian triumvirate which includes Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi and reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.
According to the constitution, the vice president must stand in if the president is incapacitated for a long period.

Anh's deputy, Nguyen Thi Binh, is not a member of the Politburo or the party's Central Committee. If Anh died, she would be expected to play only a figurehead role until a successor was chosen and put to the National Assembly for approval.
Analysts say Anh's departure could reopen an internal debate over leadership succession that simmered ahead of a key Communist Party congress earlier this year.

Muoi, Anh and Kiet represent a balance of different political hues within the party and come from the north, the centre and the south of the country. Political analysts say Anh is considered to be the most conservative of the three.

Sources said four senior Politburo members, National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh, Defence Minister General Doan Khue, Lieutenant-General Le Kha Phieu and Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam were likely candidates to replace Anh.
